Methods for zinbreg objects

zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for models fitted by zinbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3, getOption("digits") - 3), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3, getOption("digits") - 3), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("response", "count", "zero"), ...)

Arguments

x, object

An object of class "zinbreg" (or "summary.zinbreg" for the print method of a summary).

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (currently ignored).

model

For coef and vcov: "full" (both parts, the default), "count" or "zero".

type

For predict: "response" (the mean \((1 - \pi)\mu\), the default), "count" (the count-model mean \(\mu\)) or "zero" (the zero-inflation probability \(\pi\)). For residuals: "response" (y - (1 - pi) mu, the default) or "pearson" (the response residual divided by the ZINB standard deviation).

newdata

An optional data frame with the covariates at which to predict. If omitted, predictions are for the data used in the fit.

Value

  • print returns its argument invisibly.

  • summary returns an object of class "summary.zinbreg" with separate coefficient tables (estimates, standard errors, z values, p-values) for the count and zero parts; the count table includes Log(theta).

  • coef returns the coefficients, named count_* and zero_* when model = "full", and vcov their variance-covariance matrix.

  • logLik returns an object of class "logLik" whose df counts both sets of coefficients plus theta, so that AIC() and BIC() work.

  • fitted, residuals and predict return numeric vectors.

  • nobs returns the number of observations.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
mu <- exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x)
p <- plogis(-1 + 0.8 * d$z)
d$y <- ifelse(runif(n) < p, 0, rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = mu))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)

fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = y ~ x | z, data = d)
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>      1.1342      0.4486 
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial with logit link):
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>     -0.8172      0.7150 
#> 
#> Theta: 2.057
#> Log-likelihood: -944.6338 on 5 Df
#> 
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = y ~ x | z, data = d)
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  1.13416    0.06076  18.666  < 2e-16 ***
#> x            0.44855    0.05387   8.326  < 2e-16 ***
#> Log(theta)   0.72138    0.19560   3.688 0.000226 ***
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial with logit link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  -0.8172     0.1672  -4.887 1.02e-06 ***
#> z             0.7150     0.1393   5.133 2.86e-07 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 2.057  (SE 0.4024)
#> Log-likelihood: -944.6338 on 5 Df
#> AIC: 1899.268   Number of observations: 500
#> Number of EM iterations: 36
#> 
coef(fit)
#> count_(Intercept)           count_x  zero_(Intercept)            zero_z 
#>         1.1341602         0.4485549        -0.8171633         0.7149913 
coef(fit, model = "zero")
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -0.8171633   0.7149913 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1899.268
BIC(fit)
#> [1] 1920.341
nd <- data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1), z = c(1, 0, -1))
predict(fit, newdata = nd)
#>        1        2        3 
#> 1.043145 2.156204 4.003188 
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "count")
#>        1        2        3 
#> 1.984973 3.108562 4.868155 
predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "zero")
#>         1         2         3 
#> 0.4744792 0.3063661 0.1776787
